name: Vi
description: Voice set for PROJECT: Vi (skin 11): a street-smart, blunt detective who keeps the neon streets in line, with a lower-sector enforcer's toughness. Patrols, cases, statements, stakeouts and badges. Builds on vi-original.json.

messages.message: {momentTitle} is {voteDiff} down. That's a crime scene, not a deficit. Call it in.
Thirty or more behind. Time to put out an all-units call.
{momentTitle} is {voteDiff} behind. Knock on some doors. Get witnesses voting.
Fifteen-odd behind. Nothing a good tip-off can't fix.
Down {voteDiff}. Pull in a partner. Preferably one who votes.
{voteDiff} behind. Couple of leads and we're level.
Down {voteDiff}. Small case. Close it before the shift ends.
Dead level. One vote cracks the case. Find it.
One vote apart. Stakeout's over. Move in.
{voteDiff} votes between them. No suspect's cleared yet. Get more eyes on it.
{voteDiff} votes apart. This one goes to the last report.
{momentTitle} is at {userPct}%. Case practically closed.
{userPct}% and the evidence keeps piling up. Don't clock off early.
{userPct}%. Strong lead. Stay on patrol.
{userPct}% on your pick. We're ahead. Keep the pressure on.
Up at {userPct}%. Good. Now make it stick.
{momentTitle} was {voteDiff} down and just took the lead. Every cop loves a late break in the case.
{voteDiff} behind, now ahead. The late tips paid off.
Climbed out of a {voteDiff} hole. Nobody had a warrant on that comeback.
{momentTitle} was losing. Case reopened. Now it's winning.
{momentTitle} just pulled ahead. Told you to trust the instinct. Okay, I wasn't sure either.

messages: {username} voted with you on {momentTitle}. Two witnesses, same story.
{username} picked {momentTitle} too. Statements match.
{username} agrees with you. File that under rare.
Same pick as {username}. Case closed, if you ask me.
{username} backed {momentTitle}. Good instincts on the beat.
{username} went with the same one. That's corroboration.
{username} is on your side of {momentTitle}. Keep them on the roster.
{username} made the same call. No objections from the precinct.
{username} voted {momentTitle}. Solid partner material.
details: Don't let them down on shift.

messages: {username} voted {theirMoment} against {yourMoment}. Wrong suspect.
{username} picked {theirMoment}. Let's see whose evidence holds.
{username} went the other way on {yourMoment}. Wrong, but they've got nerve.
{username} voted against you. I'd argue, but the tally's a better detective.
{username} took {theirMoment}. Reckless. Dumb, but reckless in a way I respect.
{username} is against {yourMoment}. Fine. Take it outside.
{username} disagrees on {yourMoment}. Let the vote sort the statements.
{username} voted the other way. They'll need a better alibi.
details: Everybody files a bad report once.
Don't take it personally. Or take it very personally.
A rival keeps the case sharp.
They'll fall in line once the evidence lands.
At least it's a clean fight.

messages: Ten in a row with {username}. That's not luck, that's a partnership.
{username} and you, ten matches, same verdict every time. Tight squad.
Ten straight with {username}. I'd put that pair on any case.
A ten-match run with {username}. Good police work.
Ten for ten with {username}. Impressive. Keep it off the record.
{streakCount} matches with {username}. That's past a partnership, that's a task force.
{streakCount} in a row with {username}. I'd ride with you two anywhere.
{streakCount} straight picks with {username}. That's practically telepathy. Suspicious, honestly.
A {streakCount}-match run with {username}. Nothing on the books beats that.
{streakCount} with {username}. You two could run the whole precinct.
details: Hard to believe. I checked the records. It's real.

messages: Ten matches against {username}. That's an open feud now.
{username} has gone against you ten times running. They hate your taste in suspects.
Ten in a row opposite {username}. Neither of you is giving a statement.
A ten-match run against {username}. Two stubborn badges, one stalemate.
Ten times at odds with {username}. I'd sit in on that interrogation.
{streakCount} against {username}. That's not a rivalry, that's a turf war.
{streakCount} in a row opposite {username}. Neither of you yields.
{streakCount} straight disagreements with {username}. That's a standing case file.
A {streakCount}-match feud with {username}. Someone call internal affairs.
{streakCount} against {username}. I respect the dedication. Take a day off, though.
details: Neither of you is backing off.
Glad I'm not the one mediating.

messages: {matchTitle} wraps in {timeLeft} and you're still off the case. Get on it.
{timeLeft} left on {matchTitle}. No statement from you yet. File it.
{matchTitle} closes in {timeLeft}. Yours is the report missing.
{timeLeft} left on {matchTitle}. Step on it.
{matchTitle} closes in {timeLeft}. Don't make me come and cuff you to the desk.
Only {timeLeft} until {matchTitle} ends. Your report's still blank.
{matchTitle} closes in {timeLeft}. Last call, detective.
{timeLeft} left. Decide. Go.
Final dispatch on {matchTitle}. {timeLeft}. Make the call.
{matchCount} matches you haven't voted in are about to close. First one wraps in {timeLeft}.
{matchCount} unvoted cases about to close. The nearest has {timeLeft} on the clock.
No votes on {matchTitle}. Somebody take the first statement.
{moment1} against {moment2} and no one's on record. I'll wait. Briefly.
New case, zero votes. Be the first on scene.
{matchTitle} is wide open. Cordon it off and start.
{totalVotes} vote{votesPlural}. That's a thin file.
Hardly any witnesses on this one. Fix that.
Turnout's low. Come on, it's a slow beat.
Nobody's gone on record for this one. Somebody should.
details: Every statement counts when it's this quiet.
Don't let the file go cold.

messages: {matchTitle} is tied and you haven't voted. Crack it.
Dead level on {matchTitle}. One vote closes the case.
Tied. Someone has to make the arrest. Make it you.
{moment1} and {moment2}, neck and neck. Pick one.
Still tied and almost out of time. Last chance to crack it.
Level with the shift almost over. Vote.
Tied, and the clock's nearly dead. Don't stay at your desk on this one.
Round {round} is open. {matchCount} new cases. Start your shift.
{matchCount} matches just opened in round {round}. Time to patrol.
Round {round} is live, {matchCount} cases on the board.
New round. {matchCount} matches. Time to pick a suspect.
Round {round}: {matchCount} cases waiting on your report.
{momentTitle} won. Case closed.
{momentTitle} is through. Good call, detective.
{momentTitle} took it. Clean arrest.
{momentTitle} won, and it had the evidence behind it.
{momentTitle} advances. Easy case.
{momentTitle} moves on. That's police work.
details: One down, more on the board.

messages: {momentTitle} lost. That one hurts.
{momentTitle} is out. The ruling didn't go our way.
{momentTitle} didn't survive the hearing. Brush it off.
{momentTitle} went down fighting. Good effort.
{momentTitle} is out. On to the next one.
{momentTitle} lost this round. Annoying. Case not closed on us.
{momentTitle} got knocked out. We take the next case.
Still deliberating? Quit stalling and pick.
Don't overthink it. Make the call and move on.
They're all worth a look. Go with the instinct.
You've reviewed the file long enough. Pick.
details: No wrong way to pick. Plenty of ways to regret it.

messages: Welcome to the beat. {liveCount} matches are open. Pick one.
New on patrol? {liveCount} matches are live. Get on it.
Good timing. {liveCount} cases need votes.
{liveCount} cases open. Pick a suspect.
Welcome. {liveCount} matches. Show me what you've got, rookie.
Day two. You clocked back in. Good.
Two days running. Nice.
Back for day two. I noticed.
{days} days off the beat. Nice of you to show up.
After {days} days you're back. Late shift's better than none.
{days} days. Thought you'd transferred out. Glad you didn't.
{days} days away. Plenty of paperwork to catch up on.
You're back on shift. Good.
Welcome back to the precinct. Let's work.
Back already. Nice.
Hey. Cases are waiting.
First vote logged. Welcome to the force, rookie.
You picked a side. That's your first report filed.
Five votes. You're getting the hang of the beat.
Five. Not a civilian anymore.
Ten votes. The desk sergeant knows your name.
Ten. You're part of the furniture now.
Twenty-five votes. People hear you when you talk.
Twenty-five. The whole precinct listens.
details: Statement received, loud and clear. +{xp} XP

messages: Fifty votes. You're deep in the case files.
Fifty. You actually care. Good detective.
A hundred votes. They'll name a desk after you.
One hundred. Commendation-worthy. Don't tell the captain I said so.
Three days on shift in a row. That's a routine.
Three straight days. You're reliable.
details: Clocking in is half the job. +{xp} XP

messages: A full week on duty. That's dedication.
Seven shifts running. Salute.
details: A week without calling in sick. +{xp} XP

messages: Two weeks on duty. You really don't quit, do you?
Fourteen days straight. Wow.
details: Two weeks, not one missed shift. +{xp} XP

messages: Thirty days. Honestly? Thanks for the service.
A month on the beat. That counts for a lot.
details: A full month on patrol. +{xp} XP

messages: Five underdogs. You back the suspect nobody trusts.
Five long shots. Maverick style. I like it.
details: Five and still your own cop. +{xp} XP

messages: Fifteen underdogs. You pick the hard cases on purpose.
Fifteen. You don't follow the precinct line.
details: You rule on your own evidence. +{xp} XP
Fifteen votes on the long shot. +{xp} XP

messages: Thirty underdogs. Nobody can profile you.
Thirty. The long shot is your whole method.
details: Thirty votes for whoever was losing. +{xp} XP

messages: First on scene for five matches. You don't dawdle.
Five times you beat everyone to the scene.
details: You show up before dispatch. +{xp} XP
Five votes before dispatch even called. +{xp} XP

messages: Fifteen matches with you first on scene. Habit now.
First through the tape, again and again.
details: Fifteen first arrivals at the scene. +{xp} XP
Ahead of the whole shift. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten close matches. You love a tight case.
Another narrow case. Your nerves are better than mine.
Twenty-five close matches. Your vote keeps cracking the case.
You've broken it open more than once.
You stuck with the underdog five times. Stubborn detective. I approve.
You don't drop a lead because it's cold. Respect.
details: Faith in a late break. +{xp} XP

messages: Same moment, three times. Somebody's got a prime suspect.
That one again? It must be guilty of something good.
Five votes for the same moment. That's some loyalty.
You're not budging off that one. Fine by me.
details: One prime suspect, five votes in. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten votes on the same moment. That's an obsession, detective.
Ten times, same pick. I won't open a file on you. Yet.
Two rounds. You're sticking with the case.
Round two and you're still on it. Good.
Four rounds. You're deep in the investigation.
Deep in the bracket. Heavy cases ahead.
details: A long way from the first call-out. +{xp} XP

messages: Six rounds. You worked the case to the end.
All the way. You didn't clock out early.
details: First call to final report. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten matches. You check every lead.
Ten different matches. Thorough. I like it.
Twenty-five matches. You've covered the whole district.
Twenty-five. Not a corner left unpatrolled.
Fifty matches. That's not browsing, that's a career.
Fifty. You know this bracket better than the people who drew it.
Five in one sitting. Good pace for a shift.
Five back to back. Keep patrolling.
Ten in one go. Take a break. Coffee's on the desk.
Ten in one sitting. That's overtime stamina.
Voting at this hour? Night shift or insomnia?
Dead of night. Dedication, or you can't sleep either.
You put the word out. Thanks, partner.
Five shares. More witnesses, more votes.
Fifteen shares. You're basically on the squad.
Fifteen. You keep rounding up recruits. Love it.
details: Still putting the word out. +{xp} XP

messages: You were here before the precinct opened. Founding member, for good.
One of the first thousand. Nobody can take that badge.
details: That one's yours for the whole career. +{xp} XP
Nobody's prying that badge off. +{xp} XP

messages: New rank. Earned on the street.
Promoted. Don't let it go to your head.
Achievement unlocked: {name}. Good work, detective.
Another one in the case files: {name}.
{rank}. Hard-earned.
You did the work and it shows.
Ten underdogs. Reckless. Runs in the family, sadly.
Ten long shots. Not much rattles you.
details: Ten against the department odds. +{xp} XP
Long shots are your specialty. +{xp} XP

messages: Ten close ones with Cait. Your nerves are steel.
Ten tight finishes. She'd approve. I'm saying nothing about me.
Seven days alongside Cait. She's rubbed off on you.
A week without a miss. Commendable.
details: A week by her side. +{xp} XP

messages: You broke the tie. Clean arrest.
A tied match and you made the call. Good instincts.
details: The vote that closed the case. +{xp} XP

messages: Detective Vi, reporting. I've got your back.
Vi's your partner now. Don't make me regret it.

upcoming: Not open yet. Hold the line.
Voting hasn't started. Dispatch will tell you when.
prevote: Two edits, one vote. Study both, then make the call.
Watch them both before you rule. No snap judgments.
I'm not feeding you the verdict. Your case.
Take a minute. Then file it.
Go with the gut. It's usually right.
prevote-empty: No votes yet. Be the first officer on scene.
Quiet in here. Somebody start the report.
Empty so far. Make the first entry.
closing-24h: Under a day left and no vote from you. Get on duty.
closing-3h: Time's short. Vote before the shift ends.
voted-early: You voted early with barely anyone in. First on scene. Nice.
Hardly a vote in and you chose. Decisive.
voted-ahead: Your pick's ahead. Nice. Case isn't closed yet.
{pick} is pulling ahead. Good detective work.
A lead's a lead. Keep surveillance on it.
voted-close: That's close. Too close. I'm chewing my badge.
Razor margin. One more vote swings it. Get on the radio.
Tied up tight. Your pick needs backup on the scene.
{pct} to {otherPct}. Don't take your eyes off it.
voted-tied: Dead level. No suspect's cleared yet.
A perfect tie. Infuriating. Weirdly satisfying.
voted-behind: You're behind. That doesn't make you guilty.
{pick} is trailing. Underdog. My favourite kind of case.
They're ahead. You're not wrong, just short-staffed.
Down by {diff} points. Tell people. Put out the call.
Most went the other way. That doesn't close anything.
closed-won: {pick} went through. You read the scene right.
closed-lost: Your pick lost. It stings. Shake it off.
It didn't make it. Happens. Next case.
{pick} is out. Sorry. It was a decent call.
closed-tied: A tie. Neither side would cuff the other.
closed-unvoted: Voting's closed and you missed this one. More cases coming.
Match is over. {winner} took it. Next time, file a vote.

first-vote: First vote. Welcome. Every cop files a first report.
That's your first report. The paperwork gets easier.
You're on the force now. Welcome.
streak: {streak} days in a row. I see you clocking in.
underdog: You backed the suspect nobody else would. Noted.
An underdog pick. That takes nerve.
early: Early. You were first on scene before anyone else.
Few votes so far. Yours hits hard.
close: That vote moved the needle. Tight.
Razor thin. One more witness flips it.
Close case. Your vote carries serious weight.
behind: {pick} is behind. Behind isn't closed. Bring people.
Not winning yet. That means overtime.
ahead: {pick} is ahead. Don't clock off. Leads slip.
Good call, by the look of it.
default: Noted. I'm not interrogating your choice. Yet.
Vote's filed. Plenty more to see.

live-fresh: {unvoted} cases and no sides picked. Start with the one you've got a hunch about.
All cases are open. Take your pick. No rush from me.
{unvoted} to go. No pressure. A bit of pressure, sure.
live-some: {voted} closed, {unvoted} to go. Keep the pace.
You've opened the file. {unvoted} more waiting.
Good start. The rest won't solve themselves.
live-few: Only {unvoted} left. Wrap it up today.
live-one: Last case. Don't leave it hanging.
One case between you and a clear desk.
live-closing: Some of these close in {timeLeft}. {unvoted} still need your report.
Shift's running down. {unvoted} left, {timeLeft} on the clock.
Almost out of time. File your votes.
live-done: You've voted in every case. Nice work. Go check the bracket.
Nothing left on your desk. Come back when the next round opens.
live-none: Nothing's live right now. New cases soon. Go over the bracket in the meantime.
No cases open. I'm as bored as you are.
brackets-groups: Groups first. Top two from each go through. The rest get processed out.
Everyone starts in a group. Not everyone makes it out.
Watch the tables. They change quick.
brackets-knockout-soon: Knockouts coming up. Top two from each group advance.
No knockout yet. The groups have to finish first.
Patience. The knockout draws itself once the groups are done.
brackets-knockout-live: Knockouts now. Lose once and you're booked out.
Every case counts more now. Choose well.
brackets-bracket: Round by round. Lose once and you're off the board.
Follow the bracket. It closes in every round.
Every line here is a case someone voted on.
brackets-complete: That's the cup closed. Thanks for working it with me.
It's over. Good run. I'll miss the late shifts.
brackets-empty: No bracket yet. No suspects drawn.
Empty board. The draw's still pending. Soon.
Nothing filed yet. Check back later.

invite: {a} or {b}. One vote decides it. Make the call.
Two edits, one verdict: {a} against {b}. File your vote.
{a} versus {b}. Come give me your statement.
voted: I voted {pick} over {other}. What would you rule?
{pick} gets my vote over {other}. Challenge my report.
early: One of the first votes on {pick} against {other}. We need more witnesses.
First on scene for {pick} over {other}. Add your statement.
{pick} versus {other}, hardly a vote filed yet. Yours would matter.
tied: {pick} and {other} are dead level. One vote closes it.
{pick} and {other} are inseparable. Your vote can part them.
nailbiter: {pick} and {other} are {voteDiff} votes apart. Every statement matters now.
Only {voteDiff} votes between {pick} and {other}. File yours.
{pick} against {other}, {voteDiff} apart. It could break either way.
losing-close: {pick} is {voteDiff} behind {other}. A few statements turn it.
Down {voteDiff} against {other}, but {pick} can still win. Back it up.
{pick} trails {other} by {voteDiff}. Recoverable. File a vote.
losing-bad: {pick} is behind {other} by {voteDiff}. It needs backup.
Down {voteDiff} to {other}. {pick} deserves a fair hearing. Vote.
{pick} is behind {other} by {voteDiff}. Let's even the case.
winning-close: {pick} leads {other} at {pct}%, narrowly. Help it hold the line.
{pick} is ahead of {other}, {pct}%. Not secure. Vote.
{pct}% for {pick} over {other}. Thin lead. For now.
dominating: {pick} is out front of {other} at {pct}%. Come and see the evidence.
{pct}% for {pick}. {other} can't even see the tape.
{pick} leads {other} by a mile, {pct}%. File yours.
